title: Model artifact signing and provenance - RFC review notes
content:
Meeting: Platform Engineering — RFC review for model artifact signing and provenance
Date: 2025-11-05
Attendees: Aisha (owner), Daniel K., Ravi, Sofia, Ethan, (observing: security SME via recording)
Duration: 60m

Agenda:
- Quick recap of RFC goals and threat model
- Review proposed signing scheme and metadata model
- Discuss runtime verification overhead and backward compat
- Migration / rollout plan and tooling gaps
- Action items and next steps

Notes / Summary:
- RFC intent: ensure model artifacts (weights, tokenizer files, compilation caches) are cryptographically signed and accompanied by provenance metadata (build env, model source, quantization/compilation flags, MLflow run id) to provide tamper-evidence and reproducibility across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Root problem: customers and internal ops need stronger supply-chain guarantees for model integrity, especially for Private deployments and Dedicated reserved pools. Also enable quick detection of accidental packaging errors.
- Threat model agreed: untrusted storage or transit (S3 buckets, registries), compromised CI runner (limited rollback window), and insider risk. Not solving: offline air-gapped signing ceremonies (out of scope for initial RFC).

Design decisions discussed and consensus:
1) Signature algorithm: prefer ECDSA (P-256) over RSA-2048 due to smaller signature size and widespread KMS support (decision: ECDSA P-256).
2) Signing authority: integrate with customer KMS when available (Private) else use Redwood signing CA for hosted artifacts. Key usage policy must be auditable.
3) Metadata model: single JSON manifest per artifact bundle with fixed fields (artifact_id, version, created_by, build_hash, build_flags, model_source_uri, mlflow_run, quantization_profile, provenance_chain). Manifest itself is signed and stored alongside artifact.
4) Verification: runtime model loader will verify manifest signature at load time for Dedicated/Hosted. For Private deployments include a configuration flag to enforce (strict/enabled/disabled) verification. Default: verification enabled for Hosted/Dedicated.
5) Backwards compatibility: loader will accept unsigned artifacts with a warning unless account policy enforces mandatory signing. Migration plan (below).

Tradeoffs and concerns:
- Performance: signature verification adds ~1-5ms per artifact load (measured on dev infra with 100MB artifact). Acceptable for cold-start; warm caches unaffected. For extreme microservice patterns where models are loaded per-request, need caching of verification results.
- Storage: manifests add ~1-5KB per artifact. Negligible at scale.
- KMS costs & rate limits: using customer KMS increases operational complexity; need a caching layer for public-key retrieval and verification to avoid KMS throttles.
- Key rotation: must support key rotation for Redwood CA and customer-managed keys with re-signing workflow for existing artifacts or maintain a verification chain that records old public keys.

Implementation approach (actionable outline):
A) Artifact signing pipeline (CI integration):
  - New CI step (artifact-sign): packages artifact bundle, generates manifest.json, calls signing service (Redwood or customer KMS) to produce signature, uploads artifact+manifest+signature to artifact storage (S3/registry).
  - Tooling: small CLI helper (go) to run locally for ad-hoc signing by engineers (for private deployments).

B) Signing service & key management:
  - Hosted: Redwood signing service wraps Redwood CA (keys in HSM/KMS), exposes internal API for CI with RBAC. Logs every signing event to audit log (immutable).
  - Private: connector mode where CI calls local signing CLI which uses customer KMS. Provide a shim that records signed manifest hashes to optional central audit bucket (opt-in).

C) Runtime verification:
  - Model loader (C++/Rust path) will call verifier that retrieves manifest and public key (cached), verifies signature, and validates manifest fields (model hash matches). Failure modes: reject load, or fallback to unsigned allowed depending on tenant policy.
  - Add metrics and traces: verification latency, failure counts, key-cache hit rate.

D) Metadata store & UI:
  - Console: show artifact provenance view (build flags, signer, signed_at, signature_id).
  - API endpoints for querying provenance by artifact id and listing recent signing events.

Migration / Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (beta, 2 weeks): Implement signing pipeline for internal models only, Redwood-managed keys, optional verification in loader. Use internal infra for integration testing.
- Phase 2 (canary customers, 4 weeks): Enable signing for selected Hosted customers and integrate Redwood signing service with console. Add KMS connector for 2 Private customers for testing.
- Phase 3 (GA, 8 weeks): Default verification enabled for new artifacts; provide a migration tool to re-sign publicly used existing artifacts or allow account policy to require re-upload.

Open questions identified:
- Re-signing strategy for millions of previously published artifacts (batch vs on-demand). (Action: estimate scope; owner: Ravi; due: 2025-11-19)
- Legal/contract implications for Redwood-managed signing for enterprise customers (who owns the private key?). (Action: loop in Legal & Sales; owner: Aisha; due: 2025-11-12)
- How to surface verification failures to SRE/Customer Success without overwhelming paging? (Action: design alerting thresholds; owner: Daniel; due: 2025-11-17)
- Key rotation & long-term chain-of-trust UX (Action: spec key rotation model; owner: Sofia; due: 2025-11-24)

Action items recap:
- Aisha: finalize RFC text with decision notes and add ECDSA rationale; publish updated link (due 2025-11-12).
- Ravi: run artifact inventory sample to estimate re-signing workload and propose batch vs on-demand approach (due 2025-11-19).
- Daniel: prototype key-cache in runtime and measure KMS call reduction (due 2025-11-17).
- Sofia: draft key-rotation UX and policy doc for both Redwood-managed and customer-managed keys (due 2025-11-24).
- Ethan: implement minimal CLI signer for private deployment testing (due 2025-11-18).

Decisions to record in RFC metadata:
- Use ECDSA P-256; manifest + signature stored alongside artifacts; verification enabled by default for Hosted/Dedicated; Private supports customer KMS connector; unsigned artifacts allowed with warning unless account policy enforces mandatory signing.

Appendix / refs discussed during meeting:
- Prototype measurement notes: verification latency microbench included in RFC PR (see linked GitHub PR).
- Recommended manifest fields and JSON schema snippet included in RFC but will be extracted to a separate schema file before GA.

Meeting adjourned. Next sync: 2025-11-12 morning async thread to finalize legal and rollout notes.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the initial scope narrow: signing + manifest + runtime verification. Delay airtight air-gapped ceremonies until after we have customer feedback.
- Watch out for flow where signed artifact is mutated by packaging (zip vs tar) causing build_hash mismatch; ensure canonical packaging step documented.
